AI Overview

AI Mode replied:

The sky is blue because Earth's atmosphere scatters sunlight in all directions, and blue light is scattered more than other colors. 
How It Works
  • White Light: Sunlight appears white, but it is made of all the colors of the rainbow. 
  • Wavelengths: Each color travels in waves of different lengths. Red and yellow have long waves, while blue and violet have short, choppy waves. 
  • Rayleigh Scattering: When sunlight reaches Earth, it hits gases like nitrogen and oxygen in the air. Because blue light has a shorter wavelength, the gas molecules scatter it in every direction much more than longer-wavelength colors.
